question: How many times can a single sterile syringe and needle be used safely?

options.A: For multiple injections on the same patient
options.B: As many times as needed until the needle bends
options.C: For up to three patients if wiped with alcohol
options.D: For exactly one injection on one patient

explanation: Syringes and needles are single-use medical devices meant for one patient and one procedure only. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h2)

question: What is a direct consequence of having weak vital data collection systems in a country?

options.A: Doctors will have less paperwork to complete daily
options.B: Citizens will stop falling sick from infectious diseases
options.C: Hospitals will automatically receive excess funding
options.D: Health planners rely on estimates that may lead to poor interventions

explanation: Inaccurate or missing data forces decision-makers to guess where resources are needed, resulting in poorly targeted health programs. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is a major barrier that prevents teenagers from visiting clinics for contraceptives?

options.A: The high academic performance required to enter clinics
options.B: Mandatory free transport provided to all school children
options.C: A complete absence of any illness during adolescence
options.D: Fear of judgmental staff and lack of confidentiality

explanation: Many teens avoid clinics because they fear being scolded by healthcare workers or having their visits reported to their parents. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h8)

question: Why do past surgeries in the tummy make a new laparoscopy trickier?

options.A: Dense scar tissue increases the risk of organ injury during entry
options.B: The patient will require a much higher dose of antibiotics
options.C: Carbon dioxide gas cannot be absorbed through scarred tissue
options.D: Special cameras are unable to function in scarred abdomens

explanation: You're learning fast! Old surgeries leave behind scar tissue (adhesions) that can pull intestines closer to the tummy wall, making it easier to accidentally nick them during instrument entry.

question: Which health issues are most common among children in chronically vulnerable homes?

options.A: Sports injuries from gym workouts
options.B: Malnutrition, stunted growth, and infections
options.C: Rare genetic disorders found only in rich families
options.D: High blood pressure from eating too much fast food

explanation: Correct! Poverty and poor sanitation expose children to hunger, poor physical development, and frequent illnesses like malaria and diarrhea.

question: Which group of men can be affected by male sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Only individuals with chronic kidney disease
options.B: Only men over the age of sixty-five
options.C: Exclusively adolescent males
options.D: Men across various age groups

explanation: Great job! Sexual health issues aren't just for older men—younger guys can face them too, often due to stress or other emotional factors.

question: Which of the following is classified as a long-acting reversible contraceptive?

options.A: Combined oral contraceptive pill
options.B: Spermicidal vaginal foam
options.C: Subdermal contraceptive implant
options.D: Male latex condom

explanation: Implants provide continuous protection for several years while remaining fully reversible upon removal. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h6)

question: A patient with a history of getting injections from an unlicensed vendor arrives showing signs of jaundice (yellow eyes/skin). What tests should the nurse expect first?

options.A: Fasting blood sugar and lipid profile test
options.B: Complete blood count and routine urinalysis
options.C: Stool microscopy and electrolyte panel
options.D: Liver function tests and viral hepatitis serology

explanation: Jaundice is a classic red flag for liver stress. Checking liver enzymes and running hepatitis screens are our top priorities here.

question: Which structure acts like a lid to prevent food from entering the trachea during swallowing?

options.A: Thyroid cartilage
options.B: Cricoid cartilage
options.C: Epiglottis
options.D: Hyoid bone

explanation: The epiglottis folds down over the larynx during swallowing to block food and fluids from entering the airway. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T5#GNS213_U2_T5_h1)

question: Lab results show a patient has large (macrocytic) red blood cells. Which vitamin shortage should you check for first?

options.A: Vitamin B12 or folate
options.B: Vitamin D and calcium
options.C: Iron and copper
options.D: Potassium and sodium

explanation: Spot on! Vitamins B12 and folate act like master builders for DNA during red blood cell growth. Without them, the cells grow too large instead of maturing properly.

question: Which of these is NOT a normal sign of recovery after a medical abortion?

options.A: Having light spotting that tapers off over a couple of weeks
options.B: Passing blood clots along with lower abdominal cramping
options.C: A persistent high fever starting several days after misoprostol
options.D: Experiencing mild nausea that goes away within twenty-four hours

explanation: A high fever is never normal—it's a warning sign of a potential infection that needs a doctor's attention right away.

question: Which set of findings means a newborn can safely stay right with mum for skin-to-skin care?

options.A: Full-term baby, thick meconium, weak cry, and floppy
options.B: Post-term baby, bloody fluid, gasping, and stiff posture
options.C: Preterm baby, stained fluid, quiet, and limp limbs
options.D: Full-term baby, clear fluid, crying, and good muscle tone

explanation: A baby born at full term who cries well and has strong muscle tone is doing great! They don't need to be separated from mum.

question: Why can severe obesity lead to problems with ovulation in women?

options.A: Excess weight physically crushes the fallopian tubes flat
options.B: Fat tissue alters hormone levels and causes insulin resistance
options.C: High body fat stops the liver from filtering normal vitamins
options.D: Obesity causes the uterus to double in physical size

explanation: Spot on! Excess adipose tissue shifts hormone balances and sparks insulin resistance, throwing off the delicate signals needed for regular ovulation. Fantastic reasoning!

question: Which of the following is a common challenge for tele-nursing practice in developing regions?

options.A: Erratic electricity supply and poor internet connectivity
options.B: Patients refusing to use phones for any medical reason
options.C: An overabundance of advanced video monitoring equipment
options.D: Excessive physical contact between nurses and clients

explanation: Unreliable power and weak network signals frequently interrupt remote healthcare delivery in resource-constrained settings. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T12#GNS212_U4_T12_h5)

question: Why should you check for bladder fullness using a scanner or your hands before placing a catheter?

options.A: To numb the urethral canal before inserting the tube
options.B: To confirm there is an actual need to drain urine before invading sterile tissue
options.C: To measure the exact concentration of bacteria inside the bladder
options.D: To determine what size French catheter is required

explanation: Brilliant! Because catheters bring infection risks, we only want to insert one when we are certain the patient's bladder is actually holding urine.

question: Why is getting an accurate diagnosis so important before treating any vaginal infection?

options.A: All vaginal infections automatically resolve on their own within forty-eight hours
options.B: Over-the-counter creams permanently damage normal vaginal tissue if used incorrectly
options.C: Treatments vary completely depending on whether the cause is bacterial, fungal, or parasitic
options.D: Providers cannot prescribe any medication without a blood test confirming the infection

explanation: Makes total sense, right? Antifungals cure yeast, antibiotics treat bacteria, and anti-parasitics handle trich. Using the wrong drug won't help our patient at all! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h5)

question: What is the main goal of public health agencies, as opposed to a regular hospital ward?

options.A: Managing health at a population level
options.B: Training medical doctors exclusively
options.C: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: Providing surgical operations only

explanation: You've got this! While hospital wards focus on one sick patient at a time, public health agencies look at the big picture—keeping whole communities healthy and preventing disease.

question: Which viral enzyme helps convert the virus's RNA into DNA?

options.A: Protease
options.B: Integrase
options.C: DNA polymerase
options.D: Reverse transcriptase

explanation: Well done! Because HIV works 'in reverse' from RNA to DNA, it relies on an enzyme called reverse transcriptase to do the trick. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h3)

question: What special feature helps cardiac muscle cells connect and pass electrical signals quickly?

options.A: Intercalated discs
options.B: Direct bone attachments
options.C: Multiple peripheral nuclei
options.D: Lack of striations

explanation: Think of intercalated discs as special communication highways between heart cells. They let electrical impulses zip right through so your heart beats as one smooth team! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h1)

question: Which of these is the main organ responsible for our sense of touch?

options.A: The spinal cord
options.B: The peripheral nerves
options.C: The skeletal muscles
options.D: The skin

explanation: You've got this! The skin is the body's largest organ and is packed with special nerve endings that help us feel the world around us.

question: What is the main difference between structural heart disorders and electrical heart problems?

options.A: Structural disorders involve physical defects in heart valves, walls, or muscle.
options.B: Structural disorders can never be present at birth.
options.C: Electrical problems always require open-heart surgery.
options.D: Electrical problems only affect the right side of the heart.

explanation: Think of structural heart issues as physical problems with the heart's building blocks (like valves or walls), while electrical problems mess up the heart's natural wiring and rhythm. You've got this!

question: Why shouldn't patients take erectile dysfunction drugs like sildenafil (Viagra) together with organic nitrates?

options.A: It causes sudden and permanent enlargement of the prostate gland
options.B: It completely stops all normal urine production in the kidneys
options.C: It triggers rapid bone marrow suppression and severe anemia
options.D: It can cause a severe and life-threatening drop in blood pressure

explanation: Both drugs cause blood vessels to open up wide (vasodilation). Combined, they can cause blood pressure to crash to dangerous levels. Always check medication history!

question: Why is getting enough calcium so crucial for a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: To prevent the baby from developing infantile jaundice
options.B: To make the breast milk taste sweet to the infant
options.C: To ensure the infant's skin develops normally
options.D: To prevent the depletion of her own bone density

explanation: Calcium constantly flows into breast milk. If a mum's diet is low in calcium, her body will borrow it right out of her own bones to protect the milk. Protect those bones, mummies!

question: What is the main goal of rehabilitation in nursing care?

options.A: To completely cure chronic underlying pathologies
options.B: To eliminate the need for any follow-up care
options.C: To maximize a person's independence and functional level
options.D: To keep patients admitted in hospital wards long-term

explanation: You've got this! Rehab is all about helping your patients live life to the fullest and do as much for themselves as possible, even if a chronic condition is still there.

question: Why do patients who receive repeated blood transfusions end up with an overload of iron in their bodies?

options.A: Transfused red blood cells immediately break down in the digestive tract
options.B: The human body lacks an active physiological mechanism to excrete excess iron
options.C: Kidneys filter out red blood cells but trap all the iron in the nephrons
options.D: The liver actively manufactures iron whenever foreign blood is introduced

explanation: Our bodies are great at holding onto iron, but we have no natural way to get rid of extra amounts. Every transfusion adds more iron, which builds up over time.

question: Where should the surgical needle be grasped by the needle holder?

options.A: At the extreme tail end of the thread
options.B: One-third to one-half from the swaged end
options.C: Right at the very sharp point of the needle
options.D: Directly in the exact middle of the curve

explanation: Holding the needle at this position gives the best balance of control and prevents the needle from bending or breaking. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h7)

question: A patient gets confused by heavy medical jargon you used. Where did the communication break down?

options.A: During the decoding phase
options.B: During the feedback generation
options.C: During the sender's encoding
options.D: During the channel selection

explanation: Exactly! Decoding is when the listener tries to make sense of your words—complex medical terms make this step tough.

question: Unexplained facial hair growth in a female patient can be a sign of which condition?

options.A: Chronic kidney disease
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Essential hypertension

explanation: Correct! Extra facial hair (hirsutism) is often linked to higher androgen levels, which are common in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS).

question: Why do anticholinergic drugs often cause annoying side effects like dry mouth and blurred vision?

options.A: They block parasympathetic nerve signals throughout the whole body
options.B: They cause a sudden drop in the patient's blood pressure
options.C: They irritate the mucous membranes in the head and neck
options.D: They dehydrate the patient by increasing kidney urine output

explanation: Because these signals help control our body's moisture and secretions, blocking them dries things up everywhere—leading to dry mouth and blurry eyes.

question: During the final stage of bone healing, what is the main job of osteoclasts?

options.A: Forming the initial blood clot within the broken bone ends
options.B: Producing new collagen fibers to strengthen the soft callus
options.C: Resorbing excess bone tissue to restore the original bone shape
options.D: Laying down a soft cartilage bridge across the fracture gap

explanation: Think of osteoclasts as the body's sculptors. They clear away any extra, messy bone tissue laid down during healing to smooth the bone back to its normal shape. You're doing great!

question: How do relaxation and distraction techniques help reduce a patient's pain?

options.A: They destroy nociceptor nerves in the skin
options.B: They permanently change pain chemicals in the blood
options.C: They stop the liver from breaking down pain meds
options.D: They trigger nerve pathways that block pain signals at the spinal cord

explanation: Think of the 'gate control theory'—calming or distracting activities send fast signals along big nerve fibers that close the spinal gate before pain signals can reach the brain.

question: A skull pin accidentally slips out while a patient is in traction. What is your very first emergency action?

options.A: Run out of the room to find the primary doctor
options.B: Remove the remaining pins with a bedside wrench
options.C: Add more weights to the traction rope system
options.D: Manually support the head in a neutral position

explanation: Don't panic! Hold the patient's head steady with your hands first to keep the neck safe, then call for help.

question: Which electrolyte level should you watch closely when giving a loop diuretic like furosemide?

options.A: Hypomagnesemia
options.B: Hypokalemia
options.C: Hypernatremia
options.D: Hypercalcemia

explanation: You've got this! Loop diuretics make the kidneys flush out extra water, sodium, and potassium, which can lead to low blood potassium (hypokalemia).

question: What is the primary age threshold that defines early marriage globally?

options.A: Under 21 years
options.B: Under 16 years
options.C: Under 18 years
options.D: Under 15 years

explanation: Global public health and human rights frameworks classify any marriage involving a person under 18 years as an early or child marriage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h1)

question: What must the pelvic floor muscles do to allow someone to pass urine?

options.A: Relax
options.B: Vibrate rapidly
options.C: Rotate outward
options.D: Contract tightly

explanation: That's right! To pee freely, these muscles have to let go and relax so the path is open.

question: When is the second medication safety check typically performed?

options.A: While preparing or pouring the medication
options.B: When removing the drug from the storage shelf
options.C: During the morning nursing handover meeting
options.D: After the patient has swallowed the pill

explanation: The second check happens during preparation to ensure the right drug and dose are being measured out correctly. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h5)

question: A clinic pharmacy is running out of cash because staff members keep taking drugs on credit and rarely pay. What should management do?

options.A: Enforce a strict cash-and-carry policy for all individuals
options.B: Allow patients to take credit but exempt the hospital staff
options.C: Reduce the salaries of staff members who owe money for drugs
options.D: Increase the selling price of drugs to cover the unpaid credit

explanation: Strictly enforcing 'cash-and-carry' for everyone protects the fund. Allowing informal credit—even for staff—quickly drains the pharmacy's stock.

question: As a nurse, what is the most important first step when caring for a pregnant teenager?

options.A: Isolating her from her family members
options.B: Putting her on strict dietary restriction
options.C: Reporting her immediately to child welfare authorities
options.D: Building a trusting, non-judgmental therapeutic relationship

explanation: Spot on! Teens are often afraid of being scolded. Building trust makes them feel safe to come to the clinic and share what they need.

question: A patient suddenly has wild, flailing movements in one arm and leg after a stroke. Which brain area is likely affected?

options.A: The anterior thalamus
options.B: The subthalamic nucleus
options.C: The optic chiasm
options.D: The pineal gland

explanation: You got it! Damage to the subthalamic nucleus can lead to hemiballismus—a condition causing sudden, forceful, flailing limb movements.

question: Why is emotional and psychological support just as crucial as physical checks during teenage puberty?

options.A: Mental health counseling replaces the need for nutritional guidance
options.B: Rapid bodily changes often cause anxiety, confusion, and body image issues
options.C: Teenagers refuse physical examinations unless given psychological counseling
options.D: Hormonal surges permanently impair the adolescent's cognitive abilities

explanation: Exactly right! Teens go through a whirlwind of physical and emotional shifts, so offering a listening ear is a big part of good nursing care.

question: A pot of cooked rice was left on the table for 5 hours on a warm afternoon. What should be done with it?

options.A: Place the rice straight into the freezer for future meals.
options.B: Reheat the rice thoroughly on the stove to kill all toxins.
options.C: Wash the rice with clean water before serving it again.
options.D: Discard the rice because it sat too long in the Danger Zone.

explanation: Leaving food out too long lets germs multiply and make toxins that heat cannot fix. When in doubt, throw it out to keep patients safe!

question: Why might a severely anemic patient NOT show a blue skin color (cyanosis) even when their oxygen is dangerously low?

options.A: Their skin is naturally thicker and hides color changes better
options.B: Anemia causes the blood vessels to dilate and turn the skin red instead
options.C: They do not have enough red blood cells or hemoglobin to display the blue color
options.D: Their lungs absorb extra oxygen from the surrounding air

explanation: You're getting the hang of it! Cyanosis needs enough hemoglobin (the stuff in red blood cells that carries oxygen) to show that blue tint. If a patient is severely anemic, they simply don't have enough to show the color!

question: Why does running out of basic injection gear cause dangerous situations on the ward?

options.A: Hospital management will automatically close down the clinic
options.B: Staff might feel tempted to reuse single-use syringes out of desperation
options.C: Nurses will completely stop writing patient notes
options.D: Patients will refuse to take any medications

explanation: Spot on! When supplies run dry, desperate situations can lead to unsafe shortcuts like reusing disposable syringes, which puts everyone at risk.

question: A nurse listens with a stethoscope and hears moist, popping sounds at the lung bases of a patient with heart failure. What are these sounds called?

options.A: Friction rubs
options.B: Crackles
options.C: Wheezes
options.D: Rhonchi

explanation: Great job! Crackles sound just like Velcro pulling apart or bubbles popping, caused by fluid opening up those tiny air sacs.
